# callback-box — What it does

_Auto-generated from the source code by a multi-agent workflow, then verified against the code
and against the running app. Nothing in this document is written by hand._

**Generated:** 2026-08-21 · **Scope:** `callback-box/` only · paths are relative to the repository root

## Summary

Read the whole chain before quoting a number from it:

| | |
|---|--:|
| Capability statements discovered by the readers | 1024 |
| …merged away as duplicates of another statement | 357 |
| …dropped as describing capability the product no longer has | 18 |
| **Capabilities catalogued here** | **649** |
| — of those, confirmed against the source | 640 |
| — of those, flagged as unconfirmed | 9 |
| Additionally driven in the running app | 168 |
| — behaved as described | 107 |
| — did not | 4 |
| — could not be settled either way | 57 |

So **640 of 649** retained statements are source-confirmed.
That percentage is over what survived merging and dropping, not over everything the readers
found: 357 statements were folded into another as duplicates before
any verification happened, and those are neither confirmed nor flagged — they are simply gone.
Of the 168 statements also driven in the app, 57 could not be settled —
roughly a third — so an in-app check is available for far fewer capabilities than the code check.

**How to read a verdict.** Verification was deliberately adversarial: verifiers were told to
refute when uncertain, so a ❌ means *"a human should look at this"*, not *"this is definitely
broken"*. Every flag was then re-examined by three independent reviewers looking through
different lenses — does the code exist, is it reachable, does it do the whole of what is claimed.
Where a story was checked in
the running app, what the app actually did takes precedence over what the code appeared to say —
with one exception, applied once here: where the final review established that an in-app check
itself was wrong (a control that correctly renders nothing because the box held no data), the
review overrules it. Such a case says so in its verification block.

A flag is cleared only when **all three** lenses are satisfied. The lenses are not three opinions
to be averaged — they test three separate necessary conditions, so one refutation is enough to
keep a flag standing.

**What this verification does not cover.** Every capability here was checked against the source.
A subset was additionally checked by driving the running app, and that pass had real limits: the
browser session authenticates with a key that clears the box auth wall but is not the box owner,
so owner-gated surfaces — device pairing, parts of settings — returned 403 and could not be
exercised. Capabilities needing a real camera, microphone, phone, or a live Google OAuth
round-trip were not driven either. Where the running box simply held no data of the right kind,
a check could not distinguish "absent" from "empty". Those stories rest on the code reading
alone. A ✅ means the code says so and, where marked 🖥️, the app did it once on one box — not
that the capability is tested.

## Problems seen in the running app

_Noticed while checking stories in the browser, whether or not a story covered them._

**admin** — The admin page loads cleanly (no console errors, no layout breakage) and every documented section is present: Agent Engine, Claude Code, Allowed Users, Create invite link, Google Services, Telegram, Secrets, Notifications, Tailscale. BUT the browse session authenticates with CB_BROWSE_API_KEY, which passes the box auth wall without producing an owner identity (server-box-scope.ts returns early on verifyBrowseKey; resolveRequestIdentity never runs, so ctx.isOwner is false). Result: Agent Engine, Claude Code, Allowed Users, Invite, Google Services and Telegram all render 'Owner access required' in place of their data, and Secrets renders 'secrets management requires an authenticated owner session...'. There is no way for this agent to obtain an owner session (the credential store is ~/.cb-auth.json, global and off-limits), so every owner-gated story below is inconclusive rather than failed. Other observations: (1) the Secrets section renders the SAME 'requires an authenticated owner session' alert TWICE (once for boxStatus, once for machineView) — duplicated error text, worth tidying. (2) 'Add a new secret' click opens nothing at all, with no feedback — the toggle appears inert in the error state. (3) Tooling, not the app: `bin/browse open /admin` (relative-path rewrite) exits 1 with zero output; only the full router URL works. bin/browse also intermittently returns 'agent-browser exited -1: (no output)' under parallel-agent load, and `bin/browse click @ref` on the 'Create invite link' submit button dispatched no network request (a DOM .click() via eval did). Used `--session adminchk` to stop other concurrent agents navigating this browser out from under the checks.

**browse-1** — 1) /card/<dir>.attach returns 'Error loading … Failed to load: 404 Not Found' — the card-page directory view works for ordinary directories (/card/box/inbox renders the directory renderer) but 404s for an attach directory (/card/box/inbox/scan-20260429T0322-dbe99514.attach). The same path under /browse lists fine, so it is the card route's directory load that fails. 2) On a cold browser profile the browse sidebar sat on 'Loading...' indefinitely (screenshot .claude/screenshots/0027-iso-browse-root.png); a reload resolved it. Reproduced a few times during the session while several agents were hitting the same box server, so it may be contention rather than a pure bug, but the pane offers no error/retry — it just stays 'Loading...'. 3) Card-body links point at /<box>/views/<path> hrefs (e.g. /user-stories-refresh/test1/views/box/examples/people/Charles_Babbage.person.card) even though following one lands on /browse/<path>. 4) Console on /browse is clean apart from Vite HMR fallback noise. 5) Environment: bin/browse is extremely flaky when several agents share the worktree — its pre-run reaper kills other agents' agent-browser daemons, so commands die with 'agent-browser exited -1', and pages were repeatedly re-mounted mid-interaction. I worked around it with an isolated socket dir/profile plus retries; a few verdicts needed several attempts.

**browse-2** — No JS page errors and no console errors beyond Vite/React-devtools dev noise. Visible problems found while driving the page: (1) IMAGE ROTATION IS WRONG — box/inbox/scan-20260429T0246-6c66f791.attach/photo-001.image.card and box/inbox/scan-20260429T0320-15d9ae2a.attach/photo-001.image.card both carry rotation: "270"; the source JPEG is a quarter-turn off (heads to the left) but the rendered result is upside-down, the rotated <img> overflows the detail panel horizontally (it starts left of the panel edge and is clipped by the viewport), and the purple subject-bbox rectangle no longer lines up with the photo. Non-rotated image cards render correctly. (2) FAILED IMAGES SHOW NO PLACEHOLDER — an in-box image URL that 404s renders the browser's native broken-image glyph; the app's 'Failed to load' ErrorPlaceholder never appears (verified via DOM: no element with role=img/aria-label 'Failed to load', innerText has no 'Failed to load'). Repro: /browse/box/inbox/scan-20260429T0246-6c66f791.attach/attach/photo-001.jpg. (3) todo-view card 'The Plate' reports 2 cards it can't read: 'no registered schema for card type "calendar-review-job"' and 'no registered schema for card type "todo-list"' — the box holds cards of types the app has no schema for. (4) Recipe yield does not scale — at 0.5x/2x the ingredients scale correctly but the YIELD line still reads '6 servings' (base 6). (5) Extfile cards (store/reviews/*.extfile.card) show 'Couldn't load the file. It may be missing, outside the allowed roots...' because they point at an absolute path outside this worktree; the commentary block above still renders. (6) Tooling note: bin/browse in this worktree intermittently exits -1 with no output on open/snapshot/screenshot (page-ready wait); --no-wait plus retries works around it.

**browse-3** — No page errors (bin/browse errors is empty); console holds only vite HMR/React-DevTools info and [chatfsm] debug lines. /browse renders the tree (box 791 items, config 24, store 46, etc.) with a 'Select a file to view details' right pane. Card pages render cleanly. Two observations not covered by a story: (1) a `ref:` that is the whole field value (e.g. course.concept-map) renders as a clickable control, but a `ref:` nested inside a list-of-objects (question card `context: [{ref, text}]`) renders as plain StaticText with no link — refs are only linkified at the scalar-field position; (2) clicking a ref control opens the target card in a modal preview dialog rather than navigating to its /card/... URL. Also: the chat husk cards in this box carry only `session` (+ sometimes `title`) — none has a `contains` field, so the 'what the conversation contained' half of fe-chat-r1-10 has no data to render here.

**capture** — The browser profile is shared per-worktree and another agent was driving the same session during this check, so several navigations were stomped (landed on /browse/... or /dev/composer-states). Verdicts below rest on the runs that were clean. Real issues seen: (1) console error on every capture-mode open -- '[capture] Failed to load resumable sessions: ResumableCaptureListError: List resumable capture sessions failed (capture-api.ts:100)', which also lights up the nav's 'Open debug log (1 error)' badge; the capture panel otherwise renders. (2) The redirect writes the search param JSON-quoted, so the address bar reads chat?capture=%221%22 (i.e. capture="1") rather than capture=1 -- ugly for a shortcut URL a person might copy, though the app parses it. (3) On some loads the final URL was chat?session=<id> with the capture param gone and no capture panel; ChatPage's session redirect appears able to drop the param, but I could not separate this from the cross-agent navigation interference. (4) The root box-selection page (http://localhost:3210/user-stories-refresh/) redirects to /auth/login, so the box tiles were not reachable. (5) Chat composer had a leftover draft ('Please reply with exactly: pong') from another session -- not mine.

**chat-1** — Box had zero chat sessions at start (content/.callback-box/chat-session-history.json was {"sessions":[],"migrated":true} and no SDK transcripts for this worktree clone), so all history had to be created by sending short messages. Observed issues: (1) A hidden Capture sheet is always present in the chat page's a11y tree (headings 'Capture', 'Start camera', 'Exit capture' etc.), and its session bootstrap fails — the toolbar shows 'Open debug log (1 error)' with 'Session creation failed: Create session failed: 401' on a plain /chat load; the Exit capture / x buttons did not remove it from the tree. (2) Bare keystrokes when the composer is not focused are swallowed by global hotkeys and navigate the app (typing a sentence with the composer unfocused jumped to Browse pages and opened the capture sheet) — worth knowing, possibly by design. (3) 'Run /compact' from Advanced posts a visible '/compact' user bubble and the agent answered it as ordinary prose; no 'Context compacted' marker was rendered. (4) The shared browse daemon is driven by other concurrent sessions in this worktree — I had to use `bin/browse --session chat1` for an isolated browser.

**chat-2** — 1) Place chip goes stale on client-side navigation: opening a landmark-scoped chat via the Place menu or the card page's 'New' chat button leaves the header chip reading 'Place: Chat' with no 'Here:' chip, even though the URL carries contextDir=store/courses/Acids_Bases.attach. A full page load of the same URL renders 'Place: Acids & Bases' + 'Here: Acids_Bases.attach' correctly. Reproduced three times. Everything in the landmark menu (directory, curated links, Recent files) is therefore unreachable until you reload. 2) Bulk upload fails auth in dev: Add > 'Upload files...' > add two small .txt files produced 'Create bulk batch failed: Not authenticated' and both rows Failed / 'Could not register with server'. The single-file composer attach path on the same page/cookie worked fine, so the bulk endpoint appears not to accept the browse-key cookie the rest of the app authenticates with. 3) Composer draft is not scoped per chat: a draft left in one session ('[selection1] [image1] draft survives?') reappeared verbatim in a brand-new session started from a card, and typing inserted my text into the middle of it. 4) In the Recent-files card preview, 'Open as full page (new tab)' links to /test1/browse/... with no worktree prefix — a 404 under the dev router (probably fine in prod where the box is at the root). 5) Operational note, not an app bug: bin/browse's default session is shared across worktree sessions, so another agent's clicks drove my tab (page jumped to /browse/config/schedules and about:blank) until I moved to --session chat2. The daemon also intermittently returns empty output; retries were needed throughout.

**dashboard** — No page errors and no failed-to-load regions; console carries only vite HMR/React-DevTools noise. Two observations worth flagging: (1) the HeaderStrip h1 renders the box's content-directory basename — literally the word 'content' — with the absolute filesystem path beneath it, so the header reads 'content' rather than the box name 'test1' (the nav's Place chip is what actually says test1). (2) The app nav bar has no counts/badges at all: it is a Place dropdown (landmarks + Dashboard/Browse/History/Inventory) plus a User avatar menu; nothing surfaces pending questions or on-plate todos from the nav on any page, even though the dashboard body knows Questions=39 and Inbox=136. Also: SystemInfo shows version and created date but no deployed commit (no deploy-info.json in a local dev checkout), and every schedule shows Last Run 'never', so the scheduler tick log is empty and nothing exercises the tick-related UI. bin/browse needs dangerouslyDisableSandbox to launch Chromium here, and the default browse session is shared across concurrent agents — I ran in an isolated --session to avoid tab collisions.

**dev-capture-mode** — Dev harness (route only exists in dev builds). It renders four sections: pending-bubble caption gallery, failed-upload banner faces, scripted capture-status transitions, delivered capture chips, plus a live CaptureOverlay mounted against an in-memory fake CaptureApi (create/finalize/cancel are log-only no-ops). Two real problems seen: (1) every time the overlay opens, the console logs '[capture] Failed to load resumable sessions: ResumableCaptureListError' — the harness fake CaptureApi (makeFakeApi in pages/dev/components/CaptureModeHarness.tsx) implements create/finalize/cancel/upload but not the resumable-session probe, so useCaptureResume falls through to a real network call that fails; the harness therefore can never show the resume dialog. (2) In the overlay, the red CaptureErrorBanner is drawn on top of the open Device settings panel and covers the 'Camera'/'Microphone' select labels (see screenshot) — the banner and the settings sheet occupy the same strip. Camera cannot actually start in this headless browser ('Camera access failed: Permission denied'), so camera-live affordances (flip/off, photo shutter) were not exercisable. No other console errors beyond expected fake-upload failures.

**dev-composer-states** — Page renders cleanly at 1280x900: a header line ('37 realizable combinations ... 8 filtered as impossible'), a labeled card per state, and an 'Impossible combinations (filtered)' section with per-row reasons. No page console errors (only vite HMR/debug/React-DevTools noise); one recurring vite info line: '[vite] Direct websocket connection fallback' on every load. The sibling dev routes also render: /dev/capture-mode (pending-capture bubble captions: preparing/transcribing/queued/still preparing 4 min/delivered/discarded) and /dev/speech (speech menu harness, mocked slow TTS, window.__speechTestLog, live state line). Harness state cards are static: clicking the lock button inside a gallery/isolated card does not change aria-pressed (expected for a state gallery, but worth knowing). Mobile-only states (keyboard row, recording row) render blank/desktop-composer unless the viewport is phone-width - the page says so. Tooling note: bin/browse's default session was being driven concurrently by another agent in this worktree (page kept jumping to /chat and to the login page); using an explicit --session fixed it. bin/browse open with a bare app path (/dev/composer-states) failed with 'agent-browser exited -1 (no output)'; the full URL worked, and the daemon intermittently returned that same empty error requiring retries.

**dev-speech** — The harness was initially broken end-to-end: every segment went to state 'failed' with console errors `[TTS] Playback error: TTS API error 500 {"error":"mock TTS fixture missing — run: pnpm tsx scripts/gen-tts-fixtures.ts"}`. Root cause is packaging, not a missing fixture: the fixtures ARE committed at callback-box/src/webapp/test-fixtures/tts/{seg0,seg1,seg2}.mp3, but the box server runs the bundled build (callback-box/dist/cli.mjs), where `const FIXTURE_DIR = join(import.meta.dirname, "test-fixtures", "tts")` (src/webapp/tts-mock.ts:21) resolves to callback-box/dist/test-fixtures/tts — a directory the build never creates. The mp3s are not copied into dist by `tsc`, so the dev-only /dev/speech harness is unusable on any dist-run server. Worth filing. I worked around it locally by copying the three mp3s into the gitignored callback-box/dist/test-fixtures/tts/ (left in place; it disappears on a clean build). Second gotcha for future checkers: browser autoplay policy means playback only starts from a real user gesture — a scripted .click() fails with NotAllowedError; use bin/browse click. Also note the menu's control row renders in DOM/a11y order Stop, Replay, Fast-forward, while the component doc comment describes Stop, Fast-forward, then Replay below the row — cosmetic ordering discrepancy only, all controls present. No other console errors or layout breakage on the page.

**history** — Two real defects found. (1) Deep-linking a commit outside the first loaded page silently shows the wrong commit: /history/8d65fe14 (138 commits back) keeps the hash in the URL but renders the NEWEST commit (993f5e8a) in the detail pane and highlights it in the sidebar — no 'not loaded' state, no error. Deep links to commits inside the loaded 50 work correctly. (2) The `path` filter only matches box-relative paths (e.g. `config/template-versions.json`), while every file path the UI itself displays in the diff panel is prefixed with `content/` (e.g. `content/config/template-versions.json`). Passing the displayed form renders the path chip plus 'No commits found' / '0 loaded' — silently empty rather than an error. Verified against the API: history.list with path `config/template-versions.json` returns commits; with `content/config/template-versions.json` returns []. No console errors on the page (only Vite HMR/React DevTools noise). Environment note: the shared agent-browser daemon for this worktree was very flaky (many `agent-browser exited -1` with no output, ~79 daemon processes from parallel sessions); every command needed retries. That is tooling, not the app.

**inventory** — Page renders cleanly; no console errors (only Vite HMR info/debug lines). One interaction quirk: `bin/browse click @eN` on the Area-view tabs reports success but does not change the selected tab; clicking the same button via JS (element.click()) works and the treemap re-renders. Could be a browse-harness click-coordinate issue rather than an app bug, but worth noting since the tabs are custom role=tab buttons with roving tabindex. 'Refresh scan' completes without error and re-renders the same figures.

**landmarks** — Page renders cleanly, no page errors; console shows only vite HMR chatter. The test1 box has only two landmark cards (Box, Acids & Bases) and ZERO chat sessions (content/.callback-box/chat-session-history.json is {"sessions":[],"migrated":true}), so every landmark shows 'No chats here yet.' + a New chat link. chat.byLandmark and chat.placeMenu both return problems: [] — no malformed landmark cards exist to exercise the warning paths. Also note: bin/browse in this worktree is flaky — roughly every other invocation exits -1 with no output and needs a retry; and the default session is shared, so concurrent page-checking agents in one worktree steal each other's tab (I had to use --session lm).

**login** — The served login page lives at the worktree prefix (/user-stories-refresh/auth/login), not under the box segment. Visiting /user-stories-refresh/test1/auth/login unauthenticated in a browser renders raw JSON: {"message":"Route GET:/test1/auth/login not found","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404} — a logged-out user who lands on a box-prefixed /auth/login deep link sees a 404 blob instead of a sign-in form (curl with Accept: text/html gets a 302 to the worktree-prefix login, so this depends on how the request is made). Password-reset routes: /auth/reset and /auth/password-reset are not routes (302 back to login); the real one is /auth/reset-password. Unrelated: opening the chat Capture panel in the browse-key session showed 'Session creation failed: Create session failed: 401'. Tooling: bin/browse/agent-browser was very flaky this run — frequent silent exits, page-ready timeouts, and snapshot refs renumbering between calls; several observations needed retries.

**questions** — Page renders 39 pending question cards (2 confirm-type with Yes/No + optional Note, 37 text-type with Answer + Submit Answer + Dismiss). No console errors beyond normal Vite HMR chatter; no failed-to-load regions. Sections observed: INVALID (only after I planted a probe card), pending list, ARCHIVE. Minor UI inconsistency: pending entries render an h3 with the card name, but once a question is answered its archive entry drops the name heading and shows only prompt / answer / status badge. No filtering or pagination — all 39 pending questions render in one long column. Tooling note (not an app bug): `bin/browse click @eN` silently no-op'd on this page (button state unchanged, card untouched); I had to dispatch clicks via `bin/browse eval` DOM .click(). Also, the default browse session is shared with other agents in this worktree and kept navigating away mid-check — I used `--session qcheck` to isolate. Box mutations I made in the disposable worktree clone (~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1), left in place as evidence: dismissed then answered scan-20260429T0322-dbe99514_unsure-008 (two auto-commits: 'Dismiss question:' / 'Answer question:'), which also produced box/jobs/2026-08-21T20-11-05-...question-followup.job.card. A temporary malformed card (zz-broken-probe.question.card) was created to exercise the invalid branch and has been deleted.

**settings** — The settings page renders five sections: iOS Companion (Create QR + Paired devices), Password, Scan uploaders (Token name + Mint token + Uploaders + 'First-time setup on a new machine'), Google Calendar, Google Drive. MAJOR CAVEAT for this run: bin/browse's browse-key identity authenticates but is NOT the box owner — a direct tRPC probe of pairing.devices returned 403 FORBIDDEN 'Owner access required'. Every ownerProcedure-backed control (pairing ticket, device list/revoke, scan-token mint/list, calendar/drive config) therefore renders 'Owner access required' instead of its data, which is why several checks are inconclusive rather than failed. Second caveat: this box has no Google auth configured, so both Calendar and Drive sections sit permanently in their error state ('Google auth not configured. Run: cb google-auth'). Observations worth flagging: (1) the Password section renders as a card with no heading at all, just the muted line 'Sign in to manage a local password.' — visually an empty panel; (2) the tRPC 403 error payload includes a full server stack trace with absolute filesystem paths in the response body visible to the browser; (3) one navigation to /admin transiently rendered a raw JSON body {"message":"Route GET:/test1/auth/login not found",...} in the page instead of a login screen — a reload loaded /admin fine, but an unauthenticated redirect path appears able to land on a raw JSON 404; (4) clicking 'Create QR' / 'Mint token' does surface the error inline next to the button (good), but the first click of Create QR via a ref click produced no visible change at all, so the error only appeared on a real click event. Tooling note: the agent-browser daemon in this worktree was flaky throughout (repeated 'agent-browser exited -1' with empty output, empty snapshots, --full screenshots silently not full-height); commands often had to be retried. That is a tooling problem, not an app one.

## Chat

### In the web app

#### Chat scoped to the nearest landmark
✅ verified · 🖥️ confirmed in the app

> As a person using the box, I want starting a chat from a card to bind it to the nearest enclosing landmark and inherit that landmark's chat settings, so that the conversation is already scoped to the right part of the box.

Files: `callback-box/src/core/landmark/nearest.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/landmark/features.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — nearestLandmarkDir (src/core/landmark/nearest.ts) globs **/*.landmark.card and nearestDirFromDirs picks the deepest ancestor-or-self directory, defaulting to "" (box root); isBoxRelativeCardPath rejects leading / and '..'. It is called by the tRPC procedure chat.openForCard (src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts:101-113), whose UI entry point is the 'Chat'/'New' buttons in src/frontend/src/pages/card/components/OpenChatControl.tsx, rendered by CardViewPage; a new chat navigates to /<box>/chat?session=new&contextDir=<landmarkDir>&card=<path>. Feature inheritance is real: chat-control-procedures.ts reserveSession calls readLandmarkFeaturesForDir(boxRoot, contextDir) (src/core/landmark/features.ts), which reads the landmark card's navigation['chat-app'] map and merges it as seedFeatures; chat-send-target.ts does the same on send.

**In the running app** (confirmed) — From /card/store/courses/Acids_Bases.attach/Acids_Bases_Progress.progress.card the 'New' button opened /chat?session=<new>&contextDir=store%2Fcourses%2FAcids_Bases.attach&card=<that card> — bound to the nearest enclosing landmark's directory with the card already in the companion pane. The 'inherits the landmark's chat settings' half could not be distinguished: the only landmark carrying chat-app settings (Acids_Bases.landmark.card) sets narration:"off", which is also the default, so an inherited value and a default look identical.

</details>

#### Start a chat scoped to a place in the box
✅ verified · 🖥️ confirmed in the app

> As a person using the box's web chat, I want to open a chat from a landmark so the agent runs inside that directory and treats my questions as scoped to it, so that conversations about one part of the box stay in that context.

Files: `callback-box/src/core/chat/session/start.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/chat/session/prompts.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/chat/session/history.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/chat/session/recent-landmark.ts`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/chat/InteractiveChat-actions.ts`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/chat/InteractiveChat.tsx`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/session-pickers/ChatsLandmarkCard.tsx`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/hooks/useOpenLandmarkChat.ts`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/lib/place-label.ts`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/lib/display-name.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — In callback-box/src/core/chat/session/start.ts, buildBackendStartOptions calls pickContextDir and then sets cwd = path.join(boxRoot, contextDir) and appends buildLandmarkSessionNote(contextDir) to the system prompt; prompts.ts:187 emits 'LANDMARK SESSION: ... Treat the user's questions as scoped to that directory unless they say otherwise.' history.ts persists contextDir per session in the v2 session history and getDirectoryForSession/getSessionLogPath resolve the bound directory; recent-landmark.ts listRecentLandmarkChats surfaces recent chats per landmark. The web entry point exists: useOpenLandmarkChat (frontend/src/hooks) is used by PlacePill.tsx and mirrored by pages/card/components/OpenChatControl.tsx, and webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts exposes contextDir-keyed procedures (lastSessionForDirectory, nearestLandmarkDir).

Directory listings do NOT use it: status.browse in webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts builds its listing itself with parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter and returns only name/type/status/title, never touching the loader registry or typed attrs. And there is no search endpoint at all in the tRPC routers, so 'search listings' has no implementation. The story over-claims scope.

Same summaries drive the browse sidebar and the directory renderer.

**Second look — exists** (satisfied) — All five cited files exist with live code. core/file-summary.ts defines FileSummary/LoaderInput/FileLoader plus titleFromFilename; core/loader-registry.ts implements registerTypeLoader/registerPathLoader, resolveLoader with type-then-path-then-fallback dispatch, and summarize() which also lifts the global contains: field; core/loader-registrations.ts registers the real memoLoader (src/schemas/memo.ts:89) and imageLoader (src/schemas/image.tsx:159). webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts imports both, calls registerBuiltinLoaders() at module load, parses cards via loadCardFile/buildLoadContext (or reads small non-card files) and exposes files.summarize, and filesRouter is mounted at webapp/trpc/router.ts:44 (files:). It has a live client: frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts calls trpc.files.summarize (routed over POST in lib/trpc/index.ts) and feeds RecentFilesPanel, which is rendered by components/chat/ContextMenuBody.tsx. shared/card-name.ts also exists and is imported by core/card-io.ts, core/search/walk.ts and frontend view-widgets. The prior verifier's objection was about which listings consume it (scope/reachability), not about whether the code exists or is wired — that is another reviewer's lens.

**Second look — reachable** (satisfied) — There is a live, unflagged entry point: src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:44 mounts filesRouter, and src/webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts:71 exposes files.summarize as a publicProcedure that calls summarize() from core/loader-registry.ts and returns the slim FileSummary from core/file-summary.ts. On the web UI side, frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts:126 calls trpc.files.summarize.useQuery, feeding RecentFilesPanel.tsx, which renders per-file FileEntry rows with the loader-derived title/metadata; that panel is mounted by ContextMenuBody.tsx:109/177 from ChatBarChrome.tsx:137, i.e. a real menu a person in the chat UI clicks. No feature flag or unset config gates it. Whether other listings (status.browse directory listing, search) also use this path is a scope/accuracy question for another lens; my lens is satisfied.

**Second look — wording** (upholds the flag) — The summarize machinery is real (core/file-summary.ts, core/loader-registry.ts resolveLoader/summarize with type-then-path-then-fallback dispatch, files.summarize in webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts), but it is narrower than the story's wording. Typed metadata exists for exactly two card types: loader-registrations.ts registers only memo and image; every other file falls through to fallbackLoader, which returns {path, title: titleFromFilename(path)} and no attrs at all, so 'typed metadata for each file' overstates it. The benefit clause names surfaces the code does not serve: BrowsePage.tsx calls trpc.status.browse, and status.ts's browse handler builds its own listing with parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter returning only name/type/status/title, never touching the loader registry; core/search/extract.ts imports titleFromFilename but not summarize, and no tRPC search-listing endpoint consumes summaries. The sole consumer of files.summarize is frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts feeding the chat RecentFilesPanel — a chat strip, not directory or search listings. Also, summarizePath loads the whole card via loadCardFile (and reads non-card files up to 64KB), so 'without loading its full content' holds only for what ships over the wire.

**Flag review** (false-negative) — The user-facing claim is true and was watched working: the browser check (browser/browse-1.json) confirmed list rows carrying derived titles and typed metadata without opening files ('Charles_Babbage — person — active', 'briefing — briefing', directory rows with item counts). The exists and reachable lenses both cleared the story; only the wording lens refuted, and its objection is about plumbing and one extra clause, not about the capability. It is right on two narrow points: (a) the loader registry the story cites (core/loader-registry.ts + core/loader-registrations.ts, which registers only memo and image loaders) is consumed by files.summarize -> frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts -> components/chat/RecentFilesPanel.tsx, i.e. the chat recent-files strip; the browse directory listing is built separately by the status.browse handler in webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts using parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter; and (b) there is no search router at all in webapp/trpc/routers/, so 'search listings' has no implementation. Both are catalog corrections: the story stays, its file list should gain webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts, and the benefit clause should say directory and recent-file listings rather than search.

</details>

Writers stamp trailers at commit time (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:233 'Triggered-By: cb tick', cli/commands/wakeup-steps.ts:75/181/259 'cb wakeup', connectors/*.ts passing this.triggeredBy plus Pulled-By/Sent-By/Created-By, cli/commands/trick.ts:42 'Run-By: trick/<name>'); lib/git-trailers.ts (parseTrailersMulti, CONNECTOR_TRAILER_KEYS) and lib/git-log.ts parse them into HistoryCommit.trailers; CommitTimeline.tsx CommitRow renders Phase and Triggered-By into the badge row and aria-label, and CommitDetail-commit.tsx CommitTab renders phase/triggered-by/session/workflow/connector chips. It is mounted, not dead: HistoryBrowser.tsx imports both components, and it is reached from pages/HistoryPage.tsx (router.tsx:150,157) and HistoryViewCard.tsx. The earlier verifier's points (no frontend reader for 'Run-By', no writer for 'Workflow:') are about which triggers are covered/wording, not about whether implemented, wired code exists — outside this lens.

**Second look — reachable** (satisfied) — A boxholder reaches this through ordinary web-UI navigation: router.tsx registers `/history` and `/history/$hash` (HistoryPage), and links exist from the place menu (PlacePill-panels.tsx:278 'History'), card actions (CardActions.tsx:54 'View history'), MissingCardState, and the dashboard (OpsLinks.tsx, RecentActivity.tsx). HistoryPage renders HistoryBrowser -> CommitTimeline/CommitDetail, fed by tRPC `history.list` (webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts, mounted in webapp/trpc/router.ts:32) which calls getLogPaginated; lib/git-log.ts parses commit trailers via parseTrailersMulti and returns them on each commit, so CommitRow's `commit.trailers['Triggered-By']`/`Phase` badges have real data. No feature flag or config gate on the route or the components. My lens is satisfied; the earlier verifier's objection was about which triggers get displayed (coverage), not reachability, which is another reviewer's call.

**Second look — wording** (upholds the flag) — The story enumerates five trigger kinds (tick, wakeup, connector, procedure, trick), but the UI only surfaces three. CommitTimeline.tsx:156-157 reads only trailers.Phase and trailers['Triggered-By'], and CommitDetail-commit.tsx reads Phase, Triggered-By, Session, Workflow, and CONNECTOR_KEYS (Pulled-By/Created-By/Fetched-By/Pushed-By/Sent-By) — which covers cb tick (tick-helpers.ts:233), cb wakeup (wakeup-steps.ts:75,181,259), and connectors. Tricks commit with `Run-By: trick/<name>` (cli/commands/trick.ts:42) and procedures commit with `Procedure: <name>` / `Step: <id>` (core/procedure/engine.ts:163, engine-step.ts:152,184,272, engine-orchestrate.ts:104); grep over src/frontend/src finds no reader for either key, so those rows get no trigger badge or chip. The 'trace a change back to the run' clause is likewise partial: the Workflow chip/facet the UI offers (CommitDetail-commit.tsx:108, git-log.ts:230, history.ts:42) has no writer anywhere in src, and nothing links a procedure commit to its run directory. Code delivers a narrower capability than the story's literal claim.

**Flag review** (real-gap) — Confirmed against both the code and the running box. Three of the five triggers the story names work: tick (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:233 'Triggered-By: cb tick'), wakeup (wakeup-steps.ts:75/181/259), and connectors (Pulled-By/Created-By/Fetched-By/Pushed-By/Sent-By plus Triggered-By) — CommitTimeline.tsx:157 reads Triggered-By into the row badge and aria-label, CommitDetail-commit.tsx adds session/workflow/connector chips, and the browser pass saw 'triggered by cb wakeup' rows and a session chip that filters the timeline to a run. The other two are not surfaced. Procedures write `Procedure: <name>` / `Step: <id>` (core/procedure/engine.ts:163, engine-step.ts:152/184/272, engine-phase.ts:185, engine-orchestrate.ts:104) and tricks write `Run-By: trick/<name>` (cli/commands/trick.ts:42); grep over src/frontend/src finds no reader for either key, so those rows carry no trigger badge and read like hand edits in the badge column. Worse, the axis that would cover them is stale: the History filter bar's 'Workflow' facet (HistoryFilterBar.tsx:72, git-log.ts:230 getTrailerFacets, history.ts:42 `^Workflow: `) keys on the PRE-RENAME trailer name — in ~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1 the log holds 104 `Workflow:` trailers, all from commits subjected '[workflow] …' before the workflow→procedure rename, and 54 `Procedure:` trailers from current runs. So the filter offers only ancient runs (process-captures, process-news, test-echo) as options and cannot select a single procedure run made since the rename. The trailers are visible in the detail pane only incidentally: stripTrailers (CommitDetail-commit.tsx:33) doesn't strip Procedure/Step/Run-By, so they render as leftover body text rather than as chips.

Both facades re-export it: renderers/index.ts exports registerFileType/getRenderers, file-types/registry.tsx exports registerFileType/resolveFileTypeUI/fallbackFileTypeUI, and file-types/index.ts re-exports registerBuiltinFileTypes. It is wired end to end: main.tsx line 8 does `import "./renderers/setup"` (which imports all 22 renderer modules to trigger registration) and line 13 calls registerBuiltinFileTypes(); consumers actually read it — components/FileView.tsx and ExternalDocument.tsx and renderers/directory.tsx call getRenderers, components/ui/FileEntry.tsx calls resolveFileTypeUI. The earlier verifier's objection is that no single call site passes both facets at once (renderers pass `renderer`, file-types/builtins.tsx passes `listUI`), which is a wording/overclaim question, not an existence one — the shared registration code exists, is exported, imported, and mounted.

**Second look — reachable** (satisfied) — The registration API is live on the ordinary app boot path: main.tsx line 8 imports "./renderers/setup", which side-effect-imports all 24 renderer modules (each calling registerFileType from file-type-registry.ts), and line 13 calls registerBuiltinFileTypes(), whose builtins register listUI entries through the same registerFileType/shared `entries` store. Both facets are then consumed by real UI: getRenderers() drives components/FileView.tsx:346, ExternalDocument.tsx:78 and renderers/directory.tsx:81, and resolveFileTypeUI() drives components/ui/FileEntry.tsx:153 (falling back to fallbackFileTypeUI/GenericIcon). file-types/registry.tsx merely re-exports the same functions, so a contributor adding a card type reaches the capability by importing registerFileType and adding one line to renderers/setup.ts — no flag, no config, no gating. The earlier verdict's objection (that no existing call site passes both facets in one call, so half-registration isn't actually prevented) is a truthfulness/mechanism question, not a reachability one; on my lens the entry point plainly exists.

**Second look — wording** (upholds the flag) — file-type-registry.ts exposes registerFileType(selector, { renderer?, listUI? }) over one shared `entries` store, so a single call CAN carry both facets — but both are optional, and its own header comment says 'a type can register a renderer only, a listUI only, or both in one call — exactly as before, just through one function instead of two.' Nothing detects a half-registration: the only console.warn paths are duplicate type-keyed listUI collisions in registerFileType and multi-match path collisions in resolveFileTypeUI; a renderer with no listUI silently yields fallbackFileTypeUI (GenericIcon). In practice no call site pairs them: all ~20 renderer registrations (renderers/question.tsx, gsheet.tsx, image.tsx, recipe.tsx, ...) pass only `renderer`, and every `listUI:` in the tree is in file-types/builtins.tsx, so types with both still take two registrations in two files. **Flag review** (false-negative) — The capability the story names is real and reachable. file-type-registry.ts is one store with one entry point, `registerFileType(selector, { renderer?, listUI? })`, and a single call can carry both facets — its own header says so explicitly ('a type can register a renderer only, a listUI only, or both in one call — exactly as before, just through one function instead of two'). Both facades re-export it (renderers/index.ts, file-types/registry.tsx), main.tsx boots both sides (`import "./renderers/setup"` plus registerBuiltinFileTypes()), and consumers read both (FileView/ExternalDocument/directory via getRenderers, FileEntry via resolveFileTypeUI). The refutation rests on 'no existing call site passes both facets at once' — true (the ~20 renderer modules pass `renderer`; builtins.tsx is a deliberately centralized icon table of type→icon lines), but that describes where the pre-existing built-ins live, not what a contributor adding a card type can do today, which is exactly the one call the story asks for. The only genuine over-reach is the 'so that' clause implying half-registration is *prevented* — the registry warns only on duplicate type-keyed listUI collisions, so a renderer with no listUI still falls back to GenericIcon silently. But the isolation half is false. For any non-410 error it returns { error: `Calendar sync failed for ${calendarId}: ...` }, and the caller loop (the `for (const calendarId of calendars)` block around line 174-188) does `if (outcome.error) return { success: false, created, updated, error: outcome.error }` — it aborts the whole sync immediately, so remaining calendars are NOT synced and the run does not 'continue to the next one'. **Second look — exists** (satisfied) — The implementing code is real and wired. callback-box/src/connectors/google-calendar.ts defines GoogleCalendarConnector.runCalendarSync (lines ~240-287), which catches sync failures, and on a 410 (HTTPError status or a message containing '410') deletes state.syncTokens[calendarId], calls saveState, and re-invokes syncCalendar with syncToken: undefined, returning fullResync: true (which sets isFullResync for the commit message). It imports live modules — syncCalendar from google-calendar-sync.ts, loadCalendarState/saveCalendarState from google-calendar-state.ts, createGoogleCalendarService from services/google-calendar.ts — and createGoogleCalendarConnector calls registerConnector (connectors/index.ts:73) and is imported by cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts:38 and cli/commands/finalize.ts:57, so nothing here is dead code. Note for the other reviewers: the non-410 branch returns an error and the caller loop in sync() (~line 180) does `if (outcome.error) return { success: false, ... }`, aborting before the remaining calendars — so the story's 'without stopping the others' half describes behavior this code does not have; that is an accuracy call, not my lens, which is satisfied.

**Second look — reachable** (satisfied) — The entry point is real: `cb wakeup` is a registered CLI command (callback-box/src/cli/index.ts:105 adds wakeupCommand), and wakeup step 4 (src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts:38) calls createGoogleCalendarConnector(boxRoot) and then connector.sync(), which is GoogleCalendarConnector.sync() — the method containing the per-calendar runCalendarSync loop and its 410 handling. The only gate is the box-owner opt-in `googleServices.calendar` checked by isGoogleServiceAllowed (src/core/box/config.ts:69), which the owner sets from the admin UI (src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:123 → admin.updateBoxConfig tRPC, src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts:228), plus Google OAuth credentials — an owner-facing setting, not a dead flag. The 410 branch itself is unconditional inside runCalendarSync, so nothing extra hides it; whether the non-410 path actually isolates a bad calendar is a behavior question outside my lens.

**Second look — wording** (upholds the flag) — The 410 half is delivered: runCalendarSync (callback-box/src/connectors/google-calendar.ts, catch block ~lines 273-286) treats status 410 (or a message containing '410') by deleting state.syncTokens[calendarId], calling saveState, and re-running syncCalendar with syncToken: undefined, returning fullResync: true, which the caller turns into isFullResync. The isolation half is not: any non-410 failure returns { error: `Calendar sync failed for ${calendarId}: ...` }, and the caller's `for (const calendarId of calendars)` loop does `if (outcome.error) return { success: false, created, updated, error: outcome.error }` (~line 180) — it returns out of sync() immediately, so the remaining calendars are never synced and the run also skips processLocalDeletes, pushAndCleanOrphans, the final saveState, and the commit. The story's 'a calendar that errors to be reported without stopping the others' (and the evidence's 'the loop continues to the next one') describes per-calendar isolation the code does not implement; the 'so that' clause of surviving an outage without intervention holds only for token expiry, not the general error case.

**Flag review** (real-gap) — Half the story is delivered and the other half describes robustness the code does not have, with a consequence a boxholder would feel. Read `callback-box/src/connectors/google-calendar.ts` directly: `runCalendarSync` (lines ~252-283) does handle 410 as claimed — deletes `state.syncTokens[calendarId]`, saves state, re-runs `syncCalendar` with `syncToken: undefined`, returns `fullResync: true`. But the caller loop at lines 174-189 does `if (outcome.error) return { success: false, created, updated, error: outcome.error }`, so any non-410 failure on one calendar aborts the entire run: the remaining calendars are never synced, and `processLocalDeletes`, `pushAndCleanOrphans`, the final `saveState` and the explicit-path commit are all skipped — event files already written for earlier calendars are left uncommitted in the box's working tree. A calendar that fails persistently (revoked share, 403/404) therefore wedges sync for every other calendar on every subsequent wakeup, silently except for the returned error string. The story's evidence line ('the loop continues to the next one') is simply false about the code. I am classifying this as a gap rather than a story correction because the failure is a real operational one — one bad calendar takes out all of them — not a wording quibble.

</details>

Separately, for folder mounts, `syncFolder` (google-drive.ts:274-323) recreates a card for any listed Drive file whose id is absent from `existingDriveIds`, so hard-deleting a folder-mounted card makes the next sync re-create and re-sync it; the only way to stop it is removing the folder entry from config/connectors/google-drive.json — exactly the separate unsubscribe step the story's 'so that' clause denies. Files: `callback-box/src/services/google-gmail.ts`, `callback-box/src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts`, `callback-box/src/connectors/gmail.ts`, `callback-box/src/services/google-gmail-fake.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — google-gmail.ts listHistory catches a 404 from Gmail and rethrows `new NotFoundError(opts.startHistoryId, "History")` (line ~195). gmail-discovery.ts discoverGmailChanges wraps the paging loop in try/catch: `if (!(error instanceof NotFoundError)) throw error;` then re-reads `opts.service.getProfile()` and returns `{ refs: [], historyId: profile.historyId, historyResume: undefined, historyExpired: true }` — no refs, so no re-import. GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet (connectors/gmail.ts ~200) does `const state = changes.historyExpired ? resetRuleBaselines(work.state) : work.state;` plus console.warn("Gmail: history cursor expired; rule counts were refreshed without importing mail"), and persistState writes the fresh changes.historyId, re-baselining the cursor. google-gmail-fake.ts has `oldestValidHistoryId` and throws NotFoundError when start < that value.

</details>

#### Work through a large mail backlog in bounded chunks
✅ verified

> As a boxholder, I want a sync that finds thousands of changed messages to take a capped slice and carry a resume point into the next cycle, so that a big backlog drains over successive syncs instead of one run trying to do all of it.

Files: `callback-box/src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts`, `callback-box/src/services/google-gmail.ts`, `callback-box/src/connectors/gmail-state.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts discoverGmailChanges calls service.listHistory({startHistoryId, pageToken?, maxResults: GMAIL_HISTORY_RECORD_LIMIT=100}) and slices the derived refs to GMAIL_HISTORY_REF_LIMIT=500 from refOffset. When nextOffset < pageRefs.length it returns historyResume {startHistoryId,pageToken,refOffset: nextOffset} and keeps historyId at the OLD opts.startHistoryId; when the page is exhausted but nextPageToken exists it returns a resume with the next pageToken and refOffset 0; only when both are exhausted does it return page.historyId with historyResume undefined. gmail.ts syncWorkingSet passes work.state.historyResume in and persists {historyId, historyResume} via persistState, and gmail-state.ts GmailHistoryResumeSchema/GmailTransientState holds it, so a backlog drains over successive syncs.

</details>

✅ verified

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — src/connectors/transient-state.ts loadTransientState() returns defaultValue only when errnoCode(e) === 'ENOENT'; any other read error or a JSON.parse failure throws TransientStateCorruptError whose message is 'Refusing to fall back to defaults — inspect the file, or delete it to resync from scratch.' src/connectors/google-token-store.ts readTokensForUpdate() mirrors that: ENOENT -> {}, otherwise GoogleTokenStoreCorruptError ('Refusing to overwrite it — inspect or remove the file by hand, then re-authorize'). Because readTokensForUpdate is called inside the locked RMW just before writeFileAtomic (line ~202), the throw aborts the write, so a single-field update cannot replace the whole token record. #### Collect replies from a published page
❌ flagged

> As a reader of a publication with a submit block, I want to post a form on the page, so that I can send the boxholder a reply without an account or an email round trip.

Files: `callback-box/pub-worker/src/submit.ts`, `callback-box/src/publish/submission.ts`, `callback-box/pub-worker/src/index.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — The edge half exists — pub-worker/src/index.ts routes matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts), which validates fields against the manifest submit block, enforces maxSubmissionBytes/maxPerDay, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json with viewer email (null on secret) and coarseCountry. But nothing produces a page with a form: src/publish/draft.ts (draftPublication, the only manifest-assembling path, driven by `cb pub draft` in src/cli/commands/pub.ts) never sets a `submit` field and has no flag for one, and src/publish/render-docs.ts emits Markdoc HTML with no <form> element at all (grep for '<form' across src/ and pub-worker/src finds only login/invite/password pages and frontend React forms). The submit block is only a schema shape in manifest.ts/manifest-edge.ts; a reader can never encounter a form on a published page, so the story over-claims a user-reachable capability.

**Second look — exists** (satisfied) — The cited code is real and fully wired on the receiving side: pub-worker/src/index.ts:34,66-67 imports and dispatches matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit from pub-worker/src/submit.ts, which parses the urlencoded body, validates against the manifest submit block via validateSubmissionFields/submissionSchema in src/publish/submission.ts, enforces size/volume limits, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json; src/connectors/publish-submissions.ts consumes those objects and is registered live (createPublishSubmissionsConnector is called in src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts:41). The submit block is not merely schema decoration either: manifest.ts's toEdgeManifest (lines 176-189) carries submit into the edge manifest that src/publish/go.ts uploads. Nothing here is dead code. I did confirm the earlier verifier's point that no code emits a <form> (grep for '<form' across src/publish and pub-worker/src finds none, and draft.ts never sets submit), but a missing reader-facing entry point is the reachability lens's call, not mine; on existence-and-wiring the story holds.

**Second look — reachable** (upholds the flag) — The edge endpoint exists (pub-worker/src/index.ts routes matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit), but a reader has no way to arrive at it. handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts:100-105) returns 403 unless manifest.submit is non-null, and no code path ever sets that field: draftPublication (src/publish/draft.ts:202-217) is the only manifest assembler and its rawManifest has no `submit` key, and `cb pub draft` (src/cli/commands/pub.ts:80-100) exposes no flag for one. Nor is a form ever rendered — src/publish/render-docs.ts just emits Markdoc HTML, and `grep -rn '<form' src/publish pub-worker/src` returns nothing. `submit` exists only as a zod shape in manifest.ts/manifest-edge.ts, so the reader-facing entry point in the story ('post a form on the page') does not exist.

**Second look — wording** (satisfied) — Taking existence/reachability of the form as given (the other reviewer's lens), the scope claim holds. pub-worker/src/submit.ts handleSubmit accepts POST /__submit/<pubId>, validates every submitted field against the manifest's submit block via validateSubmissionFields (src/publish/submission.ts), enforces maxSubmissionBytes/maxPerDay/per-IP limits, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json; src/connectors/publish-submissions.ts pulls those objects on `cb wakeup`, safeParses them, and lands each as a pub-submission card in box/inbox/ — so the 'so that' clause (reply reaches the boxholder with no email round trip) is actually produced end to end. The 'without an account' qualifier is narrower than the general wording: resolveSubmitter returns viewer:null only for the `secret` tier, while `accounts`/`any-account` require a Cloudflare Access assertion (and, for `accounts`, allowlist membership). That is a soft narrowing rather than an over-claim — on the account tiers the reader has already authenticated just to view the page, so the accountless promise is about the secret-tier case the code does deliver.

**Flag review** (real-gap) — The receiving half is fully built and live, and the producing half does not exist, so the capability is unreachable for any reader. Confirmed directly: pub-worker/src/index.ts dispatches matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit; handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts:100-105) returns 403 unless manifest.submit is non-null; and nothing ever sets manifest.submit — draftPublication (src/publish/draft.ts:200-217) is the only manifest assembler and its rawManifest has no submit key, `cb pub draft` (src/cli/commands/pub.ts) exposes no flag for one, and `grep -rn 'submit:' src pub-worker/src` finds submit only as a zod field in manifest.ts / manifest-edge.ts and the read in submit.ts. There is also no form: `grep -rn '<form' src/publish pub-worker/src` returns nothing and render-docs.ts emits Markdoc HTML only. So the whole downstream pipeline (validateSubmissionFields, submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json, the publish-submissions connector wired at wakeup-connectors.ts:41, the pub-submission card schema) can never fire in production. This is not a wording problem: the plan (docs/plans/publish-pages.md Track F) intends a real form on submit-enabled pubs, and the resume issue's step 2 assumes a reader can submit — so the missing authoring path and form is an actual hole in a feature that is otherwise complete.

</details>

Files: `site/build.ts`, `site/render.ts`, `site/links.ts`, `site/package.json`, `.github/workflows/pages.yml`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — site/package.json defines "build": "tsx build.ts". site/build.ts main() collects site/content/**.md (collectContent), parses frontmatter via parseSource from render.ts (which throws FrontmatterError on a missing fence, invalid YAML, or a failing zod field), renders through Markdoc (renderBody), writes <stem>.html plus a <stem>.md twin (twinMarkdown) to site/dist/, then link-checks every collected internal linkTarget against the emitted set and throws BuildError('broken internal link(s)') otherwise, and finally writes llms.txt (renderLlmsTxt) plus a source manifest. parseArgs throws BuildError on an unknown flag; resolveBase falls back to baseFromBranch(git branch). .github/workflows/pages.yml runs on push to main and executes `pnpm --dir site build --base /callback-box/`, uploading site/dist as the Pages artifact.

</details>

> As an operator running several boxes on one machine, I want a box to admit only its owner or the emails it explicitly lists, so that access to one box never implies access to another.

Files: `callback-box/src/webapp/box-access.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/server-root.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — webapp/box-access.ts canAccessBox() returns true for the canonicalized owner email, else only if the box's own loadBoxConfig(boxRoot).allowedEmails (normalized) includes the email — missing/empty means owner-only, per-box config so one box's ACL never covers another. server-box-scope.ts addBoxAuthHook adds a preHandler on the /<slug> scope that ends in canAccessBox(...) → 403 'Not authorized for this box'; server-root.ts's /api/boxes handler runs the same rule through filterAccessibleBoxes. (openAccess standalone mode skips the hook, but that's an explicit operator opt-out, not the configured multi-box case.)

</details>

#### Fail closed when the credential file can't be read
✅ verified

> As an operator, I want a corrupt or unreadable credential store to make the box answer 503 rather than treat every request as unauthenticated-but-harmless, so that a damaged auth file can never quietly widen access.

Files: `callback-box/src/webapp/auth.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts`, `callback-box/src/hub/box-picker.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/capture-request-owner.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — webapp/auth.ts defines IdentitySource including "unavailable" and resolveRequestIdentity catches a throwing credential store while verifying the session cookie, logging 'failing closed (503)' and returning {email:null, source:'unavailable'} rather than a plain null/unauthenticated identity. webapp/server-box-scope.ts's box preHandler switches on identity.source and answers reply.status(503) {error:'Authentication temporarily unavailable'} for the unavailable case before any 401 path; the tRPC/WS context builder in the same file throws AuthStoreUnavailableAtContextError when source==='unavailable' and no bearer/mobile/browse key applies. hub/box-picker.ts line 84 returns the same 503 before listing boxes, and capture-request-owner.ts maps source 'unavailable' to {status:'auth-store-unavailable'} and then a rejected 503.

</details>

#### Supply the OAuth app credentials as machine secrets
✅ verified

> As an operator, I want to grant `google-oauth-client-id` and `google-oauth-client-secret` from the secret store (or set the matching env vars), so that boxes on this server can offer Google connection at all.

Files: `callback-box/src/connectors/google-auth.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/secrets/resolve.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — callback-box/src/connectors/google-auth.ts defines GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID_SECRET_NAME="google-oauth-client-id" and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_SECRET_NAME="google-oauth-client-secret" (lines 48-49) and getGoogleClientCreds() resolves both via resolveSecret({purpose:"google-oauth", access:"server"}) from core/secrets/resolve.ts, falling back to process.env.GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET only when both refusals are the benign 'no such secret' kind (refusalAllowsLegacyFallback); any other refusal returns null. In src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts, googleStatus returns {available:false,...} when creds are null and googleSetup throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST naming both secret names; the frontend consumes it in src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts. Story matches.

</details>

#### Revoking the OAuth app secret cuts the box off for good
✅ verified

> As an operator, I want a revoked or withheld `google-oauth-client-id`/`-secret` grant to leave Google simply unconfigured for that box, rather than falling through to whatever GOOGLE_OAUTH_* env vars are still exported, so that revoking a grant actually stops the box reaching Google.

Files: `callback-box/src/connectors/google-auth.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/secrets/legacy-fallback.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/secrets/resolve.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — connectors/google-auth.ts getGoogleClientCreds() resolves google-oauth-client-id and google-oauth-client-secret via resolveSecret({access:'server'}); if both ok it returns them, otherwise it computes `blocked` by asking refusalAllowsLegacyFallback for each failing half and returns null when any refusal is not fall-through-eligible. core/secrets/legacy-fallback.ts allows fallback only for kind 'unknown-secret' and warns-once for everything else; errors.ts enumerates the other kinds (not-granted, agent-access-not-granted, empty-slot, dangling-grant, store-unreadable), all of which therefore fail closed rather than reading GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET. A store id is never paired with an env secret since a partial answer either returns both from the store or falls through wholly to env. Note the store path only engages when boxRoot is supplied (box-less hub callers stay env-only), which matches the story's per-box framing.

</details>

#### Gate every box request behind the auth wall
✅ verified

> As an operator, I want each box's routes to require a recognized credential — session cookie, hub identity header, mobile device token, agent bearer, or browse key — so that box content is not reachable by an anonymous caller.

Files: `callback-box/src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/auth.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/box-access.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/auth-capabilities.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — addBoxAuthHook (callback-box/src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:67) installs a preHandler on the per-box scope that tries verifyAgentBearer, verifyBrowseKey, resolveMobileRequestAuth (device token or cb_mobile cookie), then resolveRequestIdentity from src/webapp/auth.ts (hub header or session cookie); missing email gives 401 for isApiUrl paths and loginRedirect for page navigations, and a known email failing canAccessBox (src/webapp/box-access.ts) gives 403. The only bypass is instance.openAccess, but src/webapp/server.ts refuses to listen when openAccess is true (decorate defaults to false and startServer throws), so it is a test-only seam, not a config a real deployment can be anonymous under; narrow exemptions are OPTIONS preflight, non-API static asset extensions, the diagnostic API key, and POST pairing-redeem.

</details>

## Install, deploy, and box lifecycle

### In the web app

#### Warn when a box grows unexpectedly
✅ verified

> As a person using the box, I want a health warning when my box's file, directory or commit counts jump beyond what its history suggests, and a way to say 'this is expected', so that a runaway connector or automation is caught before it buries the box.

Files: `callback-box/src/core/box-growth/health.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/box-growth/scan.ts`, `callback-box/src/core/box-growth/policy.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/health-box-growth.ts`, `callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/dashboard/HealthWarnings.tsx`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — core/box-growth/health.ts exports measureBoxGrowthIfDue (called from core/schedule/scheduler.ts:202 on the hourly tick, BOX_GROWTH_MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL_MS = 1h) and boxGrowthHealthCheck, which runs evaluateBoxGrowth (policy.ts) against BOX_GROWTH_THRESHOLDS covering absolute file/directory counts, per-hour file/directory/commit rates, and connector-specific rates, with the accepted-baseline multiplier deriving limits from the box's own prior measurement. When findings exist it returns actions acknowledge-box-growth / expect-box-growth-rates; HealthWarnings.tsx renders those as 'Acknowledge this growth' and 'Expect these rates' buttons (gated on canManageBoxGrowth, passed as isOwner from DashboardPage.tsx) wired to the mutations in webapp/trpc/routers/health-box-growth.ts (acknowledgeCurrentBoxGrowth / expectCurrentBoxGrowthRates). Commit-count findings confirmed via kind 'rate-commits' in policy.ts:165-170.

**In the running app** (inconclusive) — The 'Box warnings' section renders health-check warnings (2 pending migrations; legacy secret files) but no box-growth warning is currently firing on this box, so I could not see the growth measurement or the 'this is expected' affordance. Reaching it would require making the box grow past thresholds.

</details>

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — scanBoxInventory (src/core/box-inventory.ts) walks the box excluding .git/.callback-box/node_modules and returns per-type direct/grouped summaries with count+bytes plus repository stats; box-repository-stats.ts computes checkout/git disk bytes and an annexed-vs-regular StorageBreakdown from `git annex find` output (annexFindLine bytesize). The inventoryRouter (src/webapp/trpc/routers/inventory.ts) exposes summary with a 15-minute cache, and the /inventory route in src/frontend/src/router.tsx renders InventoryPage → InventoryContent (Git storage stats, annexed percentage, StorageTable of annexed vs regular for All/Linked/Unlinked) and InventoryTable (type, count, formatted bytes).

**In the running app** (confirmed) — /inventory shows 'Inventory summary' with whole-box totals (1,303 physical files, 111 MB content size, 1,070 grouped items), a 'Git storage' section (269 MB repository footprint, 120 MB Git storage, 99.0% logical content annexed) with an Annexed vs Regular Git table broken out by All/Linked/Unlinked showing size + file count per cell, a treemap area view (toggles All/Linked/Unlinked, Grouped/Direct, By count/By size — verified By size switches the map to '.capture-session.card 106 MB'), and a full per-type table with Type/Count/Size rows including card types (.capture-session.card 11 / 106 MB, .intake-job.card 609 / 347 KB, .question.card 39 / 22 KB, .md 115 / 230 KB, 'Orphaned .attach/' 40 / 41 KB, etc.). Card-type breakdown, file counts, bytes, and the git-annex split are all present.

#### Restart a box server without leaving a second one behind
✅ verified

> As an operator restarting a box server, I want the new process to kill the previous one for each box it serves and to exit when its own parent dies, so that a restart never leaves two servers writing to one box or an orphan holding the port.

Files: `callback-box/src/webapp/server.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/server-lifecycle.ts`, `callback-box/src/webapp/server-main.ts`

<details><summary>verification</summary>

**Code check** — callback-box/src/webapp/server.ts startServer calls resolveBoxes(options) then, for each box, killPreviousServer(path.join(box.boxRoot, '.cb-serve.pid')) before creating the server, and afterwards writes process.pid into each box's .cb-serve.pid. server-lifecycle.ts killPreviousServer reads the pid, probes with signal 0, SIGTERMs, waits 1000ms, then SIGKILLs if still alive, swallowing a stale/missing pid file. The single `shutdown` unlinks every pid file, calls server.server.closeAllConnections() and server.close(); SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP go through fireShutdown (guarded against overlapping shutdowns), and a 2000ms setInterval comparing process.ppid to initialPpid fires the same shutdown on orphaning.

</details>
