## Appendix — dropped stories

_Capability the catalog originally claimed, which review found the product no longer has (or
never had in that form). Kept here so the removal is visible rather than silent._

- **Send something out of the box by writing a card** — The story merges three card types under one mechanism the code only implements for two, and the third's real mechanism is deliberate and documented. connectors/output-cards.ts sets OUTPUT_DIR = "box/output" and deliverPendingOutputCards has exactly two callers — telegram-output-cards.ts and push.ts — so telegram-message and web-push match the story. email-outbound does not: connectors/gmail-drafts.ts findDraftCards walks only path.join(boxRoot, "box/inbox/email"), EmailOutboundSchema's own Placement section puts reply drafts in box/inbox/email/thread-X.attach/ and new mail in a fresh dir under box/inbox/email/, and schemas/email-message.tsx:70 says drafts go next to the message "not in `box/output/`". The product is self-consistent — the schema instructions an agent actually reads say the right thing — so nothing is broken; the catalog entry should be split (output-dir cards: telegram-message + web-push; email drafts: their own placement) or drop the email clause.
- **Maintain the box manifest** — The capability half is fully delivered: cli/commands/boxes.ts registers add/remove/list over ~/.config/cb/boxes.json via addBoxToManifest/removeBoxFromManifest/loadBoxesConfig (core/box/boxes-config.ts:85-121), is wired in cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(boxesCommand)), and scheduler.ts keeps the same three as deprecated aliases. The story's 'so that' clause is the wrong part: `cb serve` never reads the manifest. serve.ts's module comment says so ('feeds the SCHEDULER only — cb serve never reads it') and repeats it at the resolution site (line ~121); I grepped every loadBoxesConfig call site — scheduler.ts, activity.ts, secrets/migrate.ts, boxes.ts — and none is in serve.ts or webapp/server.ts. Multi-box serving is `cb hub` with its own hub.json (hub/hub-config.ts). So the code is fine and the story's benefit clause is stale; correct it to 'so that the scheduler knows which boxes to run' (activity.ts and secrets migrate also read it). One cosmetic loose end worth a one-line fix while someone is there, not a gap: boxesCommand's own .description() still reads 'Manage the box manifest used by serve and scheduler', which is the only place in the tree still claiming serve consumes it — the module doc-comment directly above it already contradicts it.
- **Nav bar with live pending counts** — The pending-questions badge was deliberately retired, so the story describes a removed capability. `src/frontend/src/components/AppNav.tsx:104-105` reads only `statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos` and renders PlateBadge/ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu; its bus-subscription comment says 'The question events this used to watch moved out with the questions badge.' Commit eaa86c79 ('feat(nav): single responsive bar…', Track C3 of docs/plans/top-nav-ia.md, 2026-08-02) lists 'Out: … QuestionsBadge, and the always-on chat.byLandmark fetch that fed the fresh badge' — an intentional IA decision, not a regression; pending questions surface on the dashboard's AttentionCards instead. The nav-entries half is real and reachable (core/nav.ts -> navRouter, mounted at trpc/router.ts:47, consumed by useNavMenuEntries inside PlacePill). The browser check (browser/dashboard.json) saw no badges and no box entries on test1, which matches the code given that box's data: it has no nav.card (so no box-authored section renders) and PlateBadge hides at zero on-plate todos; its ~40 pending question cards correctly produce no nav badge because none exists. Correct the story to 'the box's own menu entries plus a badge for on-plate todos'. Leftover cruft worth noting but not a user-visible gap: getNavCounts still computes `pendingQuestions` for status.navStatus with no consumer, and src/core/nav-counts.ts's header comment still claims the nav renders two badges.
- **Box subprocesses get a fail-closed environment** — The mechanism the story names is real and unconditional: pickBoxSubprocessEnv (callback-box/src/core/script-env-allowlist.ts) copies only allowlisted names/prefixes out of process.env, buildEnv (src/core/script-env.ts) always starts from it instead of a {...process.env} spread, and it adds CB_BOX_NAME/CB_SERVER_URL derived from publicUrl plus CB_AGENT_TOKEN. Two of three lenses cleared it on exactly that ground; only the wording lens refuted. What the wording lens caught is in the story's benefit clause, not the code: buildToolingScriptEnv passes connectorCreds:true, which adds CONNECTOR_ENV_ALLOWLIST (GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, CALLBACK_MISTRAL_API_KEY, THINKING_OPENAI_API_KEY, CALLBACK_OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_KEY, SKE_GEMINI_API_KEY, CB_SECRETS_FILE, CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE, CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_*) for spawns of the box's own cb tooling — including scheduled `runs:` commands, which are agent-authorable. So 'server-held secrets never leak into box-run code' is stronger than what the code has ever provided. That scope limit is not a discovery: script-env.ts's own docblock states it ('agent-reachable by writing a script card and waiting for it to fire'), and docs/implemented-plans/secret-custody.md names retiring the env-var credential path as Track 3, with the remaining steps operational (run the data migration, then remove the fallbacks). Nothing in the product is missing, broken, or unreachable — the story needs its 'never' clause corrected to describe two allowlist profiles (agent-safe for agents/tricks/chat, a wider tooling profile for the box's own cb commands, which still carries connector credentials on an env-var-configured server).
- **Invoke any box command over HTTP with its output streamed back** — All three lenses refuted, and the code agrees. The registry half is live: registerCommand/listCommands/runCommand in core/commands/, and commandsRouter (webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts) exposing list/get/executeSync, mounted at webapp/trpc/router.ts:38 — a remote script really can enumerate and run commands. The streaming half does not exist: registerCommandRoutes (webapp/routes/commands.ts), the function wired at server-box-scope.ts:262, registers exactly one route, POST /api/upload; a repo-wide grep for text/event-stream in src returns nothing; executeCommandStreaming is still exported from that file but its only importers are test/core/command-streaming.doctest.md and test/webapp/routes/ls-format.doctest.md. executeSync buffers ctx.write/writeLine into an outputLines array and returns it in the single mutation response — batched, not line-by-line. The SSE route was deliberately deleted (3fd5e4c9 removed the web-UI bare-command buttons and the execute SSE route; 898699ab removed the remaining raw /api/commands handlers as superseded by tRPC), and nothing calls the streaming helper, so no user or caller is broken. The story should be rewritten to the surviving capability (list/get/run over tRPC, output returned in the response) and drop both 'streams back line by line' and 'anything the CLI can do' (~22 registerCommand call sites vs far more CLI .command( definitions). Separately worth a code-quality note, not a product issue: executeCommandStreaming is now exercised only by two doctests for a route that no longer exists.
- **Re-transcribe an audio card using the text it already has as context** — The prompt plumbing is real but the story's scenario does not exist anywhere. In core/preactions/transcribe.ts the prompt comes from `getFrontmatterContent`, which returns `fields["body"]` (a human-typed note) and nothing else, while `applyFrontmatterTranscription` writes results into `fields["transcription"]` and never into `body` — so the prompt can never be a prior transcript. `transcribePreAction.shouldRun` also returns false as soon as `fields["transcription"] !== undefined`, so the pre-action never makes a second pass over an already-transcribed card. I also checked the one genuine re-transcription path, `cb chat retranscribe` (cli/commands/chat-audio.ts:199): it fetches the message's realtime transcript into `realtimeTranscript`, then calls `transcribeAudioHq` WITHOUT a `prompt` and merely prints the old text in the report. So no code path seeds a re-transcription with the text a card already carries. What exists — a first-pass Whisper hint taken from a typed body (transcription/index.ts pushes the multipart `prompt` field when supplied) — is a different and narrower story. Rewrite the catalog entry to that; feeding the prior transcript into `cb chat retranscribe` would be a new feature idea, not a repair of a claimed capability.
- **Run a full wakeup cycle from the web app** — The web-app trigger this story is built on was deliberately removed, and both removal sites say so in the code: webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts:16-18 ('a wakeup/connector-sync trigger procedure was removed — the box agent runs the wakeup cycle (via the scheduler / cb wakeup); the web UI no longer exposes a bare command trigger') and webapp/routes/actions.ts:28-29 ('POST /api/actions/wakeup was removed... the web UI no longer triggers it directly'). I confirmed the frontend has no replacement: no trpc.commands / executeSync caller anywhere in src/frontend/src, and the only 'wakeup' hits there are settings copy, an engine-description string, a schedule label, and DashboardPage's wakeup-complete event listener. core/commands/wakeup.ts is not dead — it is registered and reachable via commands.executeSync, and runCbWakeup's real caller is core/scan/promote-wakeup.ts — but executeSync buffers output into an array and returns it after runCommand resolves, so even that path could not deliver 'watch its output stream'; there is no command-output subscription/SSE surface in webapp/. So the code is in the intended state and the story describes a capability that was taken out: it should be dropped, or rewritten as the scheduler/`cb wakeup`/scan-promote path with an agent-scripts audience. The `triggeredBy: "webapp"` label in wakeup.ts is now vestigial and is what misled the story author; renaming it is optional tidying, not a gap.
- **Deep-link to any box surface** — The user-facing capability is real and browser-confirmed: router.tsx defines every named surface under boxLayoutRoute (/$boxSlug/{dashboard,inventory,chat,questions,browse/$,history,history/$hash,capture,settings,admin,card/$,views/$,landmarks,chats}), boxIndexRoute redirects to /chat, boxCatchAllRoute redirects to the box root, and webapp/server.ts installs an SPA fallback so a deep URL survives bookmark/reload. The browser check (browser/browse-1.json) confirmed direct navigation stays put on /browse, /browse/<dir>, /browse/<file>, /card/<path>, /landmarks, /history, /settings, with ?view=Source and /chat?capture=1&session=<uuid> round-tripping. What is wrong is the story's own qualifier: only chatRoute, historyRoute/historyDetailRoute and adminRoute (plus non-box loginRoute/setupRoute) declare a zod validateSearch; browse, card, views, landmarks, capture, settings, dashboard, inventory, questions and chats declare none and pass search through unvalidated — deliberately so for /views/$ and /browse/$, whose params are view-defined. The third cited file, lib/routing.ts, is the opposite of validation (href() returns any; toSearch() is a documented `as never` escape hatch). No product consequence: unvalidated passthrough is what those surfaces want. Fix is in the catalog — drop 'with validated query params' (or narrow it to chat/history/admin) and drop the lib/routing.ts citation. Not a false-negative: the clause as literally written is false for most routes, so the entry needs correcting rather than restoring as-is.
- **A phone voice message is upgraded to a better transcript after it is sent** — The story's headline behavior is the inverse of an intentional design, and the code is coherent. In NativeComposerView.swift the `.hq` branch does not enqueue anything: it calls `pendingStore.stageVoicePreparation`, which writes a VoicePreparation record plus a copy of the audio and nothing else. The PendingEmission is built only in `PendingEmissionStore.finishVoicePreparation`, after `prepareVoiceMessage` returns HQ text (or the 'HQ transcription failed; sending live dictation.' fallback). `rebuildDeliveries` additionally applies `preparationBarrier = voicePreparations.map(\.createdAt).min()` and skips any pending emission created after it, so later messages are held too rather than jumping the queue — ordering is deliberately preserved. Only the `.live` branch (narration off) enqueues the realtime transcript immediately. The persistence/replay half of the story is accurate (voicePreparations persist via ComposerDraftRepository, restore on activate(), and `resumeVoicePreparations` re-runs them on launch). So the catalog entry should be rewritten to what the app does — a keyword HQ send holds the message until the better transcript lands, retrying across launches — rather than 'sent immediately and then replaced'. No product defect: nothing is broken, and 'send now, correct later' would be a design change, not a fix.
- **Toggle narration and prose for a chat** — Narration is fully delivered — VoiceChip.tsx renders the 'Narration mode' item, handleToggleNarration (InteractiveChat-hooks.ts:164-194) calls setChatFeature -> chat.setFeature, and the browser check (browser/chat-2.json) confirmed the toggle flips the next turn's <chat-app narration="on"> envelope. Prose is a real, working feature but has no user control: the only literal feature name any frontend call passes is 'narration' (grep of src/frontend for setChatFeature), the frontend only consumes prose (proseEnabled), and FeatureDescriptor.uiKind / listFeatures() are referenced nowhere outside src/core/chat/features.ts, so the settings UI those fields anticipate does not exist. Prose is changed by asking the agent (prompts.ts:123-127 documents `<chat-app prose="off"/>` as a mid-conversation toggle), by turning narration on (which flips prose off), or by landmark frontmatter. Nothing is broken or unreachable — the story just bills prose as a UI toggle alongside narration when the UI has one toggle. Correct the story to 'turn narration mode on and off' and note prose rides narration / the agent. The unused uiKind+label ('Show agent prose') in the registry is dead metadata, not a user-visible defect.
- **Agent-added card fields survive a connector rewrite** — The mechanism is real, unconditional on the rewrite paths, and deliberately narrow — the story is what is wrong. `callback-box/src/connectors/preserve-agent-fields.ts` carries over a hardcoded `AGENT_FIELDS = ['contains', 'contains-evidence']`, and only when the existing value is a non-empty string and the freshly rendered template did not already set that key. Its own docblock calls these 'the fields agents own on connector-managed cards', and those two are exactly the global card fields the agent-facing docs steer agents to write (`docs/adding-schemas.md:72`: 'contains is the field agents should populate'). The call sites are unconditional (gmail-threads.ts:186 inside writeThreadCards, drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, drive-handler-docs.ts:321 — the story omits the docs handler). So the design is 'template owns the card, these two named fields survive', not 'anything an agent adds survives', and the story's unqualified 'the fields I added ... aren't erased' describes a capability that never existed. Fix the catalog entry to name the two preserved fields (and the third call site); no product change is warranted. Worth noting without inflating it into a gap: `todos` is also a global card field (`src/cards/schema.ts:87-92`) and is a list, which the `typeof value !== 'string'` guard skips, so a todo attached to a connector-managed card would not survive a sync — a narrow, speculative case, not something observed.
- **Read box history to see what each sync changed** — The described behavior is real for the connectors the story actually describes; the word 'every' is the part that is wrong, and it is a catalog fix rather than product work. Confirmed: `gmail-commit.ts` `buildGmailCommitMessage` renders 'Pull N Gmail thread(s) (M files)' with capped New:/Updated: lines and `gmail.ts:178` commits it with `Pulled-By: gmail-connector` plus a conditional `Triggered-By`; `google-calendar-notes.ts` `buildNarrativeCommitMessage` turns `describeChanges`' field-level SyncNotes into the body, `google-calendar.ts:225-231` commits an explicit changed-file list with the same trailers and falls back to 'Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)'; `src/lib/git.ts:378-381` really renders trailers. The exception is Drive: `src/connectors/google-drive.ts:211-214` commits `Sync Google Drive: N new, N updated, N pushed` with no `trailers` object, even though the class declares `triggeredBy` (line 82); `telegram-webhook.ts:70-74` sets `Pulled-By` only. So every connector sync does get a written summary — the benefit clause ('git history explains external changes instead of opaque file churn') holds across the board — but the connector/trigger attribution is a per-connector convention, not universal. I am not calling the missing Drive trailers a gap: the commit subject already names the connector, so the reader-facing consequence is close to nil; it is a one-line consistency wart worth mentioning to the maintainer, not a user-noticeable break. The catalog entry should be narrowed to Gmail and Calendar.
- **Connect Google from whatever URL the box is served at** — The story's headline mechanism (redirect built from the browser's own origin) is dead in practice and the project has explicitly decided against it. googleSetup (src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts:49-64) accepts an optional `origin`, but the sole caller — src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:93 — calls `mutate({})`, and a repo-wide grep for `googleSetup` (src/, ios-app/, callback-clerk/, doctests) turns up no other caller. What actually runs is resolveBoxPublicUrl: config/box.json#publicUrl -> CB_PUBLIC_URL/PUBLIC_URL -> http://localhost:3210 (src/lib/public-url.ts), slug-stripped by baseServerUrl (src/webapp/base-server-url.ts). That is not a shortfall: issues/bugs/2026-07-28-google-oauth-pairing-broken.md (Update 2 + 'Latent smell') records the maintainer conclusion that deriving an OAuth redirect_uri from a client-supplied origin is a smell to remove, because every alternate origin (dev router, Tailscale URL, alternate subdomain) yields an unregistered redirect_uri Google rejects — the canonical configured URL is the wanted behavior, and it is what runs. The 'so that' clause is satisfied through box.json publicUrl / CB_PUBLIC_URL, not through the browser origin. So the code is fine and the story misdescribes it; the catalog entry should say the redirect is built from the box's configured public URL (box.json -> env -> localhost), slug-stripped. The dormant `origin` input is cruft already tracked in that issue, not a missing capability.
- **Flip a draft live behind a human confirmation** — The safety gate the story exists for is intact and correctly described everywhere but one clause: goPublication (publish/go.ts) reloads the manifest, re-reads the on-disk bundle, re-runs scanBundle, refuses unaccepted findings ('leaks-blocked'), then calls deps.confirm ?? defaultTtyConfirm, which returns false outright when !process.stdin.isTTY and otherwise requires the answer to equal the pub-id exactly; a false answer short-circuits to reason 'not-confirmed' before any store.put, and uploads put bundle objects first with manifestKey last. cli/commands/pub.ts's goCommand injects no confirm, so the TTY prompt is the real default path. The false clause is 're-show the file-by-file preview': defaultTtyConfirm prints tier, expiry, slug, allowlist, `bundle files: N` and a leak-finding count — it never enumerates paths, sizes or hashes. The per-file printPreview() in pub.ts runs on the `go` path only in the leaks-blocked branch, i.e. when the flip is already refused. This matches the design rather than falling short of it: docs/plans/publish-pages.md:148 puts the file-by-file listing (path, bytes, sha256) on `cb pub draft`, and line 150 puts the eyeball surface on the authed /publish-preview/<pub-id>/ route. So the code is fine and the story over-specifies; correct it to 'shows the publication's tier/expiry/allowlist and file count and requires the typed pub-id at a TTY'. One inaccurate in-code comment feeds the same misreading and is worth a one-line fix, not an issue: pub.ts's comment above the goPublication call says the default confirm 'displays the preview + tier/expiry/allowlist'.
- **Give a Codex chat the box's own guidance** — The story misnames the channel; the capability is delivered by design. `expandClaudeIncludes` (src/core/agent-context-includes.ts) reads CLAUDE.md only to match `^@file.md` lines and pushes just the included files' bodies into `sections` — CLAUDE.md's own text is never appended — so codex-chat.ts:47-58 folds the includes, not CLAUDE.md, into `developer_instructions` (codex-sdk-session.ts:174). That split is deliberate: Codex reads AGENTS.md natively, and `mirrorClaudeDocs` (src/core/agent-context-mirrors.ts:50-61) symlinks AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md beside every CLAUDE.md in the package; what Codex does NOT do is resolve Claude's `@file.md` includes, which is exactly the hole expandClaudeIncludes fills. I verified the mirror is live and self-healing: generateAgentContextMirrors is called from ensureAgentContext (src/core/docs-gen/claude-md.ts:16), and generateDocs runs at chat start (src/core/chat/session/start-run.ts:116) and in the reactor loop; the worktree box ~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1 has the AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md symlink at package root, and the chat cwd (boxRoot = <package>/content, start.ts:122) sits under it. So a Codex chat does get the box's CLAUDE.md plus its includes — just not both through developer_instructions. The story should be corrected to name both halves (the @-included files go into developer instructions; CLAUDE.md itself reaches Codex through the generated AGENTS.md mirror). No product change is warranted. Aside, not a gap: the long-idle ~/src/boxes/test1 has no AGENTS.md because docs-gen has not run there since the mirror landed; it would be created on the next chat start.
- **Manage a chat session's lifecycle and settings** — Eight of the nine enumerated verbs are real, wired and browser-verified (browser/chat-1.json exercised sessions, history, defaultSession, features, label, status, statusAll, setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, reserveSession, deleteSession, sessionAvailability against the running server, and drove the session list, model menu, Stop agent, restart and delete controls through the UI). 'Rename it' has no implementation: chat-session-procedures.ts:126 `label` is a read-only publicProcedure .query over titleForSession, chat-session-procedures.ts contains no mutations at all, and there is no setLabel/renameSession/setTitle procedure anywhere in src/webapp or src/core/chat (the only rename hits are fs.rename and a husk.ts comment). There is no UI path either — ChatHuskView renders the title as static text with Open/Delete only, and the sole card mutation the frontend wires is trpc.card.trash. The verb never existed, so the catalog entry should drop 'rename it'; the code is in its intended state for what it does ship. Not classified real-gap because the missing capability is already filed and prioritized: issues/features/2026-07-20-chat-thread-management.md ('Chat thread management: delete, rename, archive', priority important) records that delete shipped via worktree-chat-session-delete and that the issue stays open for rename and archive. A new issue would duplicate it; if the maintainer wants the audit to add anything, it belongs as a note on that item.
- **Open the chat UI in one round-trip** — The code is fine and the goal is met; the story's payload list is wrong by one item. chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts returns exactly {kind, sessionId, history, label, status} — it resolves the session via getMostActive, loads history, and reads status in one query, and the browser check (browser/chat-1.json) watched a single chat.bootstrap?batch=1 call render the transcript. There is no place field in the ChatBootstrap union, and there cannot be: place context comes from chat.placeMenu (chat-place-menu-procedure.ts), which PlacePill.tsx:127 runs with `enabled: switchOpened` and ChatPage warms from idle only AFTER bootstrap settles. That laziness is deliberate and documented in both file headers — the bar is not supposed to pay for the menu at rest — so nothing is broken and nothing should change in the product. The catalog entry should drop 'and place context' (or say 'session id, history and status'), leaving the no-waterfall benefit clause intact, which the browser check confirms. Not a false-negative: the story enumerates a specific payload and one enumerated item is provably absent, so leaving the wording as-is would misdescribe the API.
- **Keep the box I have open from being stopped underneath me** — Code is fine; the story's scope is wrong. The server half is general (webapp/routes/api.ts registers `server.head("/api/keepalive")` inside the box scope, 204 + no-store, skipping health checks) and Supervisor.ensureRunning/touch do reset lastActivity and re-arm the idle timer. But both senders are gated on the dev bundle: useDevWorktreeKeepalive.ts returns immediately unless `import.meta.env.DEV`, and wakeDevBox in lib/trpc/index.ts does the same with the comment "This stays dev-only; production hubs keep their existing upgrade behavior". That gate is not a defect: lazy start / idle-stop is the dev router's model (hub-config.ts `lazy` defaults to false, and docs/implemented-plans/boxes-as-packages-v2.md records that production hub.json keeps `lazy: false` because schedulers and webhooks want children resident, with supervisor.ts's header saying the same). So in every configuration that ships, the only environment with an idle timer to refresh is the one where the heartbeat runs. The story's 'a person with a box open in a browser tab' should read 'a developer with a worktree box open in the dev router'; there is nothing to build. (A hub deliberately configured `lazy: true` in production would send no heartbeat, but that is an unused opt-in config, not the shipped path.)
